title: Protocol for formation, staining, and imaging of 3D breast cancer models
author: Haspels, Kuijten

steps.title: EdU incorporation
steps.instruction: Add EdU to the culture medium at 3 µL per mL (final concentration 30 µM) and incubate spheroids for 2 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Harvest and initial centrifugation
steps.instruction: Collect spheroids as described in steps 25‑28, transfer to a 1.5 mL low‑binding Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min at 20‑22 °C.

steps.title: PBS wash and fixation
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant, add 1 mL 1× PBS, centrifuge 100 × g for 5 min at 20‑22 °C; discard PBS, add 1 mL 2 % PFA and rotate for 30 min at 20‑22 °C.

steps.title: Post‑fixation washes
steps.instruction: Wash spheroids three times with 1 mL 1× PBS for 10 min each on a rotation wheel at 20‑22 °C, centrifuging at 100 × g for 5 min between washes. (Optional: leave overnight in PBS at 4 °C.)

steps.title: First blocking/permeabilization
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL blocking solution (1× PBS + 1 % v/v Triton X‑100 + 3 % m/v BSA) and rotate for 1 h at 20‑22 °C.

steps.title: Click‑IT reaction
steps.instruction: Remove blocking solution, add 1 mL freshly prepared Click‑IT reaction mix, and incubate 2 h at 20‑22 °C in the dark on a rotation wheel.

steps.title: Post‑Click‑IT washes and second block
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min at 20‑22 °C, discard mix, wash twice with 1 mL blocking solution for 10 min each (rotate at 20‑22 °C, protect from light), centrifuge between washes; then add fresh blocking solution and rotate 4 h at 20‑22 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Remove blocking solution, add 1 mL primary antibody diluted in blocking solution (optimize dilution), and rotate 24–48 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min at 20‑22 °C, discard antibodies, wash three times with 1 mL 1× PBS + 0.1 % m/v BSA for 10 min each on a rotation wheel at 20‑22 °C, centrifuging between washes.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Remove wash buffer, add 1 mL secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution, and rotate 3 h at 4 °C on a rotation wheel.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 100 × g for 5 min at 20‑22 °C, discard antibodies, wash three times with 1 mL 1× PBS for 10 min each on a rotation wheel at 20‑22 °C, centrifuging between washes.

steps.title: Mounting and imaging
steps.instruction: Remove PBS, add 15–20 µL Vectashield mounting medium containing DAPI, incubate overnight at 4 °C, then transfer spheroids to a μ‑slide for imaging, protecting from light.

description: Breast cancer is the most common type of cancer in women worldwide and approximately 20% of patients develop metastatic disease, which is very difficult to treat. This emphasizes the importance of studying treatment response in breast cancer in a physiologically relevant model. Use of 3D cell models has great advantages over conventional 2D cell culture, as 3D models are more physiologically relevant and better comparable to an in vivo tumor.1 This protocol describes the formation, harvesting, immunofluorescence staining and imaging of spheroids and rod-shaped micro-tissues using MCF7 and MDA-MB-436 breast cancer cells. In addition, we used MCF7 cells stably-transfected with several reporter plasmids to show the potential of this protocol without any staining procedures. For formation of 3D models we used commercially available molds (MicroTissues) in various shapes and sizes and initially used the manufacturer’s manual, which we further optimized and expanded for our applications.Note: Although we describe in this protocol the use of breast cancer cell lines MCF7 and MDA-MB-436 only, we have also successfully used these methods for A549 (lung cancer) and DU145 (prostate cancer) cell lines. Imaging of these 3D models was performed with a Leica TCS SP8 confocal microscope. General use of this microscope is not described in this protocol and can be found on the website of Leica Microsystems.1.Perform all steps for formation and harvesting of 3D micro-tissues aseptically in a flow cabinet.2.Prepare all materials and reagents in advance and make sure everything is sterilized when applicable.3.Cells are cultured in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 injection (90%–95% humidity).
